quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
Half the width of a lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: When backing up:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not depend only on mirrors because they cannot show the area directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all other vehicles coming toward you with a green light.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Put one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you while driving.
Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning ahead for hazards, not just staring at the car directly in front of you. Watch the road ahead and be aware of vehicles around you.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, lift your foot off the gas and avoid braking. Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, press your brakes firmly and steer straight ahead.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Overtaking cars.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles driving straight. You can only turn when it is safe and does not interfere with traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: When stopped at a red traffic light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: First come to a complete stop.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can proceed in that direction if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear of pedestrians and other vehicles. You do not need to wait for other signals.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending. Be ready to change lanes or adjust your position.

questions.question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance work areas:

options.text: Have a red background with green writing.
Have an orange background with black writing.
Have a yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black text and symbols.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a pedestrian who is using a white cane or a guide dog?

options.text: Honk your horn so they know to clear a path.
Yield the right-of-way.
Swerve quickly around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, be cautious and courteous. Allow them to safely cross before you proceed.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?

options.text: Immediately enter the right lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up and enter only after you see a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter only after you see a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, speed up only after you find a gap in traffic. Wait stopped for a gap to appear.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol?

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows all nerve impulses and bodily functions. It reduces inhibitions and hurts your ability to concentrate and stay alert.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave first.
Only if pedestrians are not texting.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to yield to any vehicle or pedestrian in the intersection. You may proceed carefully only if your lane is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area set aside for construction workers.
The area where pedestrians can cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians can cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are often marked with white solid lines to show where pedestrians should cross. They may have additional lines between or instead of the parallel lines. Crosswalks can also be unmarked.

questions.question: When used on roads, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles when used on roads. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for merging traffic if you can.
Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When safe, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if your brakes fail.

questions.question: You reach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights. What should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning devices, or flaggers warn you of a train. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions right ahead. This sign warns of an upcoming right curve.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park.
Point your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: On a hill, always use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the center of the road so the car rolls safely if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn toward it when going downhill, or touch it gently when going uphill.

questions.question: When turning left from a one-way street, which lane should you be in?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: To turn, use the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, be in the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights coming toward you, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward whichever edge is nearest to you.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points, but first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Flash your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If visibility is very poor, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror removes all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
Your rearview mirror shows all blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots you cannot see. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: When driving on ice or snow, you should:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to keep traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before steep hills to prevent skidding. Keep more distance behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid sudden stops. Pump your brakes unless you have antilock brakes.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slow.

questions.question: A five-sided sign is:

options.text: A stop sign.
A regulatory sign.
A school zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about school zones. It tells you that children and pedestrians may be crossing nearby.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must go either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must go either right or left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road splits and you must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: When do large trucks lose speed?

options.text: When driving up long or steep hills.
When driving in long, gradual curves.
When driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks accelerate more slowly than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going up long or steep hills. When driving behind a large truck, give it extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. It frustrates other drivers and causes them to make dangerous passing moves. Drive with the flow of traffic within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large commercial vehicle?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They vibrate and make noise to alert sleepy or careless drivers that their vehicle has left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They vibrate and make noise to alert sleepy or careless drivers that their vehicle has left the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or careless drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance between vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance between vehicles.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and do not tailgate.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell you?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
It is not safe to pass.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: "No passing zone" signs mean you cannot pass in that area. You are in an area with poor visibility where passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving behind a motorcycle?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three to four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely endangers both drivers. If a motorcycle falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting the rider. Falls are most common on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.
When there is a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a red traffic light. You must always follow orders from police officers directing traffic, even if signs or signals say differently.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
A divided highway is ahead.
Two-way traffic is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming conditions. This sign warns that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night on a dimly lit street?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep the instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This makes your vehicle roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so the vehicle rolls into the curb if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When daylight starts to fade, what should you use to help others see you?

options.text: Parking lights
Low beam headlights
Emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights
questions.explanation: As daylight fades, turn on your low beam headlights so others can see you. Only use high beam headlights in open areas with no other drivers present.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front of you moves right to let you pass
When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken
When the yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes
Look below their headlights
Look toward the right edge of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night, as it will blind you. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway
So the truck driver has room to stop the vehicle
So other drivers have space to slow down

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop the vehicle
questions.explanation: Trucks take much longer to stop than cars, even at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead
Passing is not allowed from either direction
Passing is allowed from either direction

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separating traffic lanes means any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Water on the road causes hydroplaning. At what speed can your car start to hydroplane?

options.text: 45 miles per hour
35 miles per hour
40 miles per hour

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires push water away from the tire. When you drive faster than 35 mph, tires cannot push water away as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?

options.text: Turn on your turn signal
Slow down
Brake hard

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the posted speed limit based on road conditions. You must never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down for curves, hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Steer off the road
Drive in a low gear
Steer and brake smoothly

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid hard braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there isn't enough room on the other side to completely cross the tracks
When the crossing is in a city with frequent train traffic
When you are transporting two or more young children

questions.correctAnswerText: When there isn't enough room on the other side to completely cross the tracks
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time in either direction. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop. Do not stop while crossing the tracks.
